glossary.definition: The API does not remember previous calls. You must send the full conversation history every time you make a new request.
A limit you set on how many tokens the model can generate in its reply. Use it to control cost and prevent very long responses.
A field in the response that tells you why the model stopped generating — for example, it finished naturally, hit the token limit, or wants to call a tool.

hook.scenario: You see three different code shapes for calling GPT in three different blog posts. Before reading further, predict: which field in the response object contains the text you actually want?
hook.question: Hold your guess, then read on to learn the one canonical shape and the two response fields that matter most.

mental_model.intuition: One function call with a `messages[]` list in, one message object out. Every other feature — streaming, tools, structured output — is just one more parameter on top of this single shape.
mental_model.description: The chat completions API is the single interface for almost all LLM work: text generation, extraction, classification, agents, and RAG answer generation. It takes a list of role-tagged messages, sends them to a model, and returns the model's reply as another message object. Once you know this shape, every other feature is just one extra parameter.

sections.body: The request has three required things: a model name, a `messages[]` list, and your API key (passed when you create the client). The messages list is ordered: system first (optional but standard), then alternating user and assistant turns. Every call is stateless — you resend the full history each time. The model only sees what is in this list.
sections.recap: Request = model + `messages[]`. Stateless — send the full history on every call.

sections.body: The response object has a predictable shape. `choices[0].message.content` is the text you want. `choices[0].finish_reason` tells you why the model stopped: `'stop'` means it finished naturally; `'length'` means it hit `max_tokens`; `'tool_calls'` means it wants to call a tool (and `message.content` will be `None`). `usage.total_tokens` is what you were billed. Ignore everything else for 90% of use cases.
sections.recap: Response: `.message.content` = text. `finish_reason` and `usage.total_tokens` are the two other useful fields.

sections.body: Key optional parameters: `max_tokens` caps output length — always set this, because uncapped replies can be very long and expensive. `temperature` controls randomness (0 for factual, 0.7 for creative). `n=2` gives you two independent completions for the same prompt, but doubles the cost. `response_format={type: 'json_object'}` asks for JSON output — but does not validate the schema (more on that in the structured-output lesson).
sections.recap: Always set `max_tokens`. Temperature and `response_format` are the two other everyday levers.

sections.body: Error handling is not optional in production. The API returns HTTP error codes: 400 (your messages list is wrong or over the context limit), 401 (bad API key), 429 (rate limit — wait and retry), 500/503 (server error — retry with backoff). The `openai` SDK raises typed exceptions. Catch them specifically rather than catching all errors silently.
sections.recap: 400 = your bug (do not retry). 429 = rate limit (retry with backoff). 500 = server (retry with backoff).

code_snippets.title: The minimal canonical call — learn this shape by heart
code_snippets.code:
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI()  # reads OPENAI_API_KEY from environment

response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='gpt-4o',
    messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'What is idempotency?'}],
    max_tokens=200,
)
text = response.choices[0].message.content
print(text)
code_snippets.explanation: This is the shape every other feature builds on. `OPENAI_API_KEY` is read from the environment — never hardcode keys. `max_tokens` prevents expensive runaway replies. The response `.content` is a plain string.

code_snippets.title: Inspect what you were billed and why the model stopped
code_snippets.code:
response = client.chat.completions.create(
    model='gpt-4o',
    messages=[{'role': 'user', 'content': 'List 50 countries in Europe.'}],
    max_tokens=100,   # intentionally short to show truncation
)

print(response.choices[0].finish_reason)   # 'length' — hit max_tokens, not done
print(response.usage.prompt_tokens)        # tokens in the input
print(response.usage.completion_tokens)    # tokens in the output
print(response.usage.total_tokens)         # what you are billed
code_snippets.explanation: `finish_reason='length'` means the model was cut off mid-answer — raise `max_tokens` or redesign the prompt. `finish_reason='stop'` means it finished naturally. Log `usage.total_tokens` in production to catch runaway costs early.

code_snippets.title: Production wrapper: error handling and retry logic
code_snippets.explanation: Use exponential backoff on 429 and 5xx errors — wait a little longer after each failed attempt. Never retry 4xx errors (except 429) — those are problems with your request that will not fix themselves on their own.

common_mistakes.title: Not setting max_tokens
common_mistakes.explanation: Without `max_tokens` the model can generate a very long response. This is slow and expensive. For tasks where you know the output size (classification = 1 word, summary = 3 sentences), cap it tightly.

common_mistakes.title: Reading response.choices[0].text instead of .message.content
common_mistakes.explanation: The `.text` field is from the old `/v1/completions` endpoint. The chat completions response uses `.message.content`. Reading the wrong field returns `None` or raises an `AttributeError`.

recall_questions.q: Explain the chat completions API to a classmate who has never used it before.
recall_questions.answer: You send a list of messages — each with a role (system, user, or assistant) and some text. The model reads them and replies with a new message. Every call is independent; the model only knows what you include in this list.

recall_questions.q: What does finish_reason='length' mean and how do you fix it?
recall_questions.answer: The model hit the `max_tokens` cap and was cut off before finishing. Fix: raise `max_tokens` or redesign the prompt to get a shorter answer.

recall_questions.q: Which HTTP status codes should trigger a retry, and which should not?
recall_questions.answer: Retry: 429 (rate limit) and 5xx (server errors) with exponential backoff. Do not retry 400 (bad request — your bug) or 401 (bad key) — those will not fix themselves.

recall_questions.q: What happens if you remove max_tokens from your production call?
recall_questions.answer: The model can generate a very long reply. This raises your cost and increases response time. Some inputs may trigger very long outputs without warning, making your app slow and expensive.

oa_questions.question: A production LLM pipeline occasionally returns None for the response text. Logs show no exceptions were raised. What are two likely causes?
oa_questions.answer: The response text is `None` in two known cases. First: the code is reading `response.choices[0].text` (the old completions field) instead of `response.choices[0].message.content`. Second: the model returned a tool call response (`finish_reason='tool_calls'`), and `.message.content` is `None` when the model wants to call a tool. Always check `finish_reason` before reading content.
oa_questions.approach: Two classic `None` causes: wrong field name (`text` vs `message.content`) and `tool_calls` finish reason. Check `finish_reason` defensively in production code.

oa_questions.question: Your pipeline's average response time doubles overnight. Token usage also spiked. What API parameter might explain this?
oa_questions.answer: `max_tokens` was likely removed or raised to a very high value. LLM response time grows with output token count, not just input. Without a cap, some inputs can trigger very long replies, inflating average time and cost. Check that `max_tokens` is set to a reasonable value for your task.
oa_questions.approach: LLM latency scales with output tokens. Missing `max_tokens` is the most common cause of sudden latency and cost spikes.
